checked.comment: Stochastic K-armed model with rewards in [0,1]; the paper lists n and K as known parameters.
Section 4 treats the K-armed case against an adaptive adversary, with rewards in [0,1]^K.
Section 3: two arms against an oblivious adversary.
Two-armed stochastic model with Delta = |mu_1 - mu_2|.
SAO (Algorithm 4.1) maps to registry id sao. Its parameter beta depends on n, and the algorithm uses K.
SimpleSAO maps to registry id simple_sao. Its parameter C_crn = 12 ln n needs the horizon n.
Matches Theorem 1.1(a). The bound is on E[R_n] against the best arm in hindsight, so expected_regret is the right quantity.
Matches Theorem 1.1(b). oR_n is defined through the means, so pseudo_regret is correct, and Delta in the paper is the minimal gap.
Matches the high-probability stochastic bound of Theorem 4.2, with beta = 10Kn^3/delta substituted correctly.
Matches the high-probability adversarial bound of Theorem 4.2 exactly as printed in the theorem.
High-probability version of Theorem 3.1(a), holding with probability at least 1 - 1/n.
High-probability version of Theorem 3.1(b), holding with probability at least 1 - 1/n.

summary: The extraction is accurate. It covers Theorems 1.1, 3.1 and 4.2 with the correct settings, quantities, constants, beta substitutions and registry ids, and I found nothing to correct. The remaining theorems, lemmas and claims are concentration tools or intermediate steps of the proofs and were rightly left out, and the cited results are recorded faithfully.
